To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two plants Veronica anaggallis-aquatica L and Epilobim laxum L were successfully used for cadmium phytoextraction.

the addition of fertilizer and plant growth regulators to the media significantly increased growth and biomass of both plants, while cadmium accumulation in the plants increased significantly in the presence of fertilizer, GA3, and IAA.
both plants have the potential to remove cadmium from contaminated water, however, Veronica plant has more ability than Epilobium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of Veronica and Epilobum for cadmium removal from contaminated water and to be used as an alternative to conventional treatment methods.
the use of two plant species Veronica anagallis aquatica and Epilolobium laxum to remove the cadmium from polluted water.
the use of two aquatic plants to enhance phytoextraction of Cd from water and to investigate the role free proline and phenolics on Cd phytoextraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of plant growth regulators in combination with fertilizers could be used as an effective tool for the enhancement of phytoremediating ability of aquatic plants.
the use of Veronica plant in combination with GA3 and NPK foliar sprays could be a potential candidate for cadmium phytoextraction from polluted water.
the use of NPK and GA3 as a fertilizer and plant growth regulator respectively in combination, enhanced the phytoremediative potential of both plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of fertilizers and growth regulators to the hydroponic media and foliar spraying of growth regulators to the plant leaves significantly enhanced the cadmium phytoextraction potential of the plants.

the addition of NPK fertilizer and GA3 in combination (foliar spray) to the hydroponic media is an important factor in enhancing plant growth, biomass, and Cd accumulation in the plants, and the role of phenolic and proline contents was found positive for cadmium accumulation in the plant.
the addition of fertilizer and plant growth regulators in the media and foliar spray of plant growth regulators can increase growth, biomass, and Cd phytoaccumulated in plant tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of plant growth regulators and fertilizer application to the growth medium of plants can significantly improve their ability to accumulate heavy metals from contaminated water.
both plants are able to accumulate Cd, but the Veronica anagallis aquatica is the best choice for Cd phytoremediations of polluted water.
Veronica plant is a good candidate for the phytoremediations of cadmium-contaminated water.
